claims.text: The FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are initially solid.
Cu has a lower melting point than the other constituents of the FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Heating uncoated FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles causes Cu atoms to segregate to their free surfaces.
Surface Cu enrichment locally lowers the melting temperature of the nanoparticles.
The locally reduced melting temperature initiates premelting at the free surface.
After surface initiation, a premelting front propagates inward through the nanoparticle.
An inert surface-passivation layer prevents or reduces Cu segregation to the nanoparticle surface.
Reducing Cu surface segregation delays the onset of the melting transition.
Uncoated nanoparticles will begin premelting at a lower temperature than otherwise identical passivated nanoparticles.
Uncoated nanoparticles will exhibit a detectable Cu-rich surface layer relative to passivated nanoparticles.
Premelting onset differences can be observed using DSC and in situ TEM, while surface Cu enrichment can be quantified using XPS.
The controlled comparison uses passivated and uncoated particles heated in vacuum with an identical temperature ramp of 0.5–1 K/min.
The proposed interpretation assumes that passivation does not independently change thermal conductivity enough to affect melting.
The proposed interpretation assumes that passivation does not impose mechanical constraints that independently affect melting.
